evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: The requested capability is clear and does not rely on overloaded terms that could lead to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: The intent (listing profiles of attendees) is straightforward and not materially open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website for info and updates
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “from the website” entails (internal messaging vs. email integration), and what “for info and updates” means (content, triggers, audience scope).

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: “Very clear map” is vague and can be interpreted in materially different ways (interactive vs. static, level of detail, accessibility, accuracy requirements).

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself ... and links to slides
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “training node” includes and what “and links to slides” means (add links? edit existing? required fields?), allowing different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what counts as a “registration” (training vs summit vs camp), and what “per day” refers to (event day vs calendar day vs training day).

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status ... if attendend, refunded, no show
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous which statuses are supported and how they are determined; “helps track” is underspecified and can lead to different interpretations of required functionality.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous waitlist behavior (automatic promotion, ordering rules, notifications, per-session vs global waitlist).

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “cancellation terms” are (where defined, versioning) and when/where the checkbox is required in the flow.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: “Whatever workflow exists” is explicitly unclear; multiple materially different workflows could satisfy this, changing requirements significantly.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Conditional phrasing makes the requirement unclear (feature may or may not exist), and “my schedule” behavior is not defined (what items, how added/removed).

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: The requested information (user’s registered trainings) is clear and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: have a view ... that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: “All attendee information” is ambiguous (which fields, privacy constraints), and the story mixes multiple intents, enabling different interpretations of scope.

evaluations.evidence: all trainee information is shown and can be filtered
evaluations.rationale: “All trainee information” is ambiguous (which data elements), and filtering requirements are underspecified beyond one example.

evaluations.evidence: possibly a map view
evaluations.rationale: Most fields are specified, but “possibly a map view” is ambiguous (optional vs conditional, and what qualifies as a map view).

evaluations.evidence: clearly marked for the following information: day and time ... register now link
evaluations.rationale: The list of required information is explicit enough to avoid materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page with an intro section ... and promote call for trainings
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “intro section” contains and what “promote call for trainings” means (banner, CTA, submission form link, timing).

evaluations.evidence: have a link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: A homepage link to the training list is a clear, single interpretation requirement.

evaluations.evidence: where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Location and opening hours are concrete information needs with little room for materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether this is full vs partial refunds, single vs bulk, and whether it includes updating internal records vs only Stripe action.

evaluations.evidence: become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “$350 level sponsor” entails (benefits/role assignment) and what “become a sponsor role” means in the system.

evaluations.evidence: attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “associated with this company” means (employer field, sponsorship purchaser, email domain, manual linkage).

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “identify myself as” requires (company selection/creation, verification) and what constitutes the $350 sponsorship in system terms.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: “Maintain venues” is broad and can mean materially different operations (edit fields, deactivate, manage rooms, addresses, maps).

evaluations.evidence: view venue details ... and see the events happening there
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what counts as “venue details” and what “events happening there” includes (sessions, trainings, summits; time window).

evaluations.evidence: sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous association rule (sessions presented by sponsor attendees vs attended by them vs linked via company), leading to different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “registration process” refers to (camp vs sponsorship vs training) and what constitutes “third step” (depends on defined steps).

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: The action (assign sponsors to specific content types) and outcome (featured on sponsor detail page) are clear enough for a single interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: The listing of sponsored items for a sponsor is a clear requirement with minimal interpretive variance.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous payment specifics (authorization vs capture timing, error handling, stored payment methods) and scope of “individual sponsorship.”

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “link attendees” means (display attendee list? endorsements? association mechanism), enabling materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: “User profile” update scope is ambiguous (which fields editable, privacy controls), allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup is a commonly understood, single-interpretation capability.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “for consumption by Drupal Planet” requires (specific taxonomy, feed inclusion rules, metadata), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is clear at a high level and does not introduce materially different interpretations by itself.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading blog content is a clear, single interpretation requirement.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit that matches my brand
evaluations.rationale: “Matches my brand” is subjective/vague and can be interpreted in materially different ways (filtering, recommendations, tagging).

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Summit registration is a clear action with a single primary interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: “Detailed directions” is vague (map vs step-by-step, transit modes, starting point), allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Listing the user’s registered summits is clear and not materially open to interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: communicate with my attendees by email
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether this means exporting emails, sending bulk email from the system, templates, and which attendees qualify (registered vs waitlisted).

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: “Basic information” is undefined and can vary materially (title/description vs venue/time vs agenda/speakers).

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “list sponsors” entails (ordering, levels, logos/links, which sponsors qualify) and where it is displayed.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous agenda structure (time slots, sessions, speakers), edit capabilities, and display requirements, leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous definition of “seats left” (capacity minus registrations vs minus confirmed payments; handling cancellations/waitlist).

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: “Specific details” is vague and can include materially different sets of information (agenda, venue, sponsors, directions, registration).

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: A list of summits is a clear requirement with minimal interpretive variance.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: The intent to present sponsorship level information is clear; while details could expand, the term is not materially ambiguous in this context.

evaluations.evidence: WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what qualifies as “long-form content” and which content types are included, leading to different scope interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: The linkage from job listings to a sponsorship profile is a clear, single interpretation requirement.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “learn about” entails (FAQ page, pricing, rules) and who/what “the sponsorship person” is (role, contact method).

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous job posting workflow and constraints (fields, approval, duration, eligibility as sponsor), allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a job board is a clear capability with a single primary interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous relationship among room, time slot, and location (room already implies location; could mean venue vs building), enabling different data models.

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the schedule is a clear high-level requirement and not materially ambiguous on its own.

evaluations.evidence: final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “final” means (after which cutoff, includes withdrawals?) and what “approved” encompasses (accepted vs scheduled).

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Bulk-setting sessions to an accepted status is clear and not materially open to interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Setting a session’s status to accepted is a clear, single interpretation action.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “evaluated” means (accepted/rejected decision, scored, reviewed) and notification channel/timing.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous notification channel and trigger definition (on form submit vs after moderation/creation), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what parts of a session are editable and under what conditions (before/after submission, after acceptance).

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp, so that I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether “register to speak” is separate from “submit a session” (account creation vs speaker profile vs submission), leading to different flows.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session for evaluation is a clear intent with a single primary interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: “Personalize” is vague and can mean materially different capabilities (edit text, upload logo, change layout/colors, add links/media).

evaluations.evidence: list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “when they are” means (date only vs date+time vs duration/timezone), affecting displayed data requirements.

evaluations.evidence: offered several choices of idividual sponsorship on the second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “registration” refers to and what constitutes the “second page”; “several choices” is also vague about number and types.

evaluations.evidence: easily find a link in the menu
evaluations.rationale: “Easily find” is subjective and can be interpreted in materially different ways (placement, labeling, prominence, number of clicks).

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: Completing a registration form to create an account is a clear, single interpretation requirement.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: “Session information” is underspecified and could mean materially different content (title/abstract, schedule, room, speaker bio, track, slides).
